title: Session slab throttle + resume token coalescing action plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-03-04 a customer workload spike plus an internal batch test triggered slab-level throttling in the edge proxy pool. Multiple proxies had heterogeneous resume-window configuration and inconsistent slab eviction timing. The result was frequent streaming disconnects, production clients receiving partial token sequences, and token duplication during client reconnects. Total affected requests peaked at ~6k/s over 18 minutes; a subset of chat sessions experienced truncated final tokens and required resend logic in the client. Impact was primarily hosted API customers using long-poll streaming and a single enterprise customer on Dedicated who ran a burst training job the same morning. This ticket captures follow-ups, design decisions, and the action plan to prevent recurrence.
mitigations_done: 2026-03-04 10:22: emergency increase of proxy slab capacity on edge-pool-eu (manual scale) to reduce eviction churn
Enabled temporary 10s extended resume-window on all proxies to allow clients to reconnect without losing in-flight tokens
Applied rate-limiter bump for the offending customer via account-level quota override; contacted customer about scheduling bursts
observability_changes: Add counter: streaming_resume_failures{proxy,region} (counts failed resume attempts where resume_token mismatch detected)
Add histogram: in_flight_token_duration_ms (measure time between token emission and ack from client)
Dashboard: streaming-resume-health (per-proxy resume success %, resume latency, slab-eviction-rate) linked to runtime runbook
Alert: slab_eviction_rate > 1/min across >20% of proxies for 2 minutes => Sev2 paging
action_items: (Marco) Implement idempotent token envelope: attach monotonic sequence id + crc to each chunk so replays/duplicates can be deduplicated by clients and proxies — ETA 2 wks
(Lena) Standardize resume-window config across all edge proxies and publish config validation in CI (infra config lint) — ETA 1 week
(DevOps) Introduce proxy-slab backoff policy that coordinates with autoscaler (prevent immediate eviction cascade) — ETA 3 weeks
(SRE) Create synthetic canary that simulates a 10k/s streaming burst with reconnects to validate resume-path under load — ETA 2 weeks
(Observability) Implement streaming-resume-health dashboard and on-call playbook entries with runbook links — ETA 5 days
(PM) Coordinate with top-affected customers to recommend burst scheduling and offer short-term dedicated capacity during migrations — ETA ongoing
(QA) Add regression tests for partial-token handling, including token-fragment replay and client reconnect flows — ETA 2 sprints
(Security) Confirm token-envelope design doesn't introduce new attacker-controlled fields; minimal review required — security_review_required=false
comments: 2026-03-05 — Aisha: Initial writeup and severity assessment. Root cause points to two factors: slab eviction cascades on overloaded proxies + inconsistent resume-window config. Filed ENG-23988 to track fixes.
2026-03-06 — Marco: Prototype for token envelope dedupe completed (branch feature/token-envelope). Draft PR to follow; needs design review from Reza for client-side compatibility.
2026-03-07 — Reza: Reviewed token-envelope design; suggested adding sequence gaps metric and fallback path for legacy clients. Added notes to Confluence doc.
2026-03-08 — SRE (Lena): Deployed config lint for proxy resume-window; found 7 misconfigured proxies in staging and 2 in prod (immediate fix applied).
2026-03-10 — DevOps: Began design of slab backoff policy. Decision to coordinate with autoscaler to drain before eviction. Need cost analysis for reserved headroom (assigned to Tomas).

2026-03-12 — PM (Carmen): Notified top-affected enterprise customer; agreed to provide a short maintenance window and test fixtures for their integration team. Customer asked for SLA credit; Support owns follow-up.
2026-03-14 — Marco: Opening PRs for token-envelope and proxy resume-window uniform rollout. Scheduling canary run on 2026-03-16 during low-traffic window. Marking ENG-23988 In Progress.
Review notes: Design requested clear versioning of token-envelope so clients can opt into new protocol; backward compat will be supported for 3 months.
risk_assessment: Medium-high until token-envelope and slab backoff are deployed. Residual risk is miscoordination during rollout leading to temporary increased resume failures; mitigated by staged canary with abort conditions and automated rollback.
acceptance_criteria: List: 1) Resume success rate >99.9% under synthetic 10k/s burst with reconnects, 2) slab-eviction-rate alert suppressed in canary, 3) dashboards and runbook published, 4) token-envelope rollout tested with 2 major SDKs and backward compat validation
notes: Keep communication thread open with Support and Customer Success during rollout. Capture any customer-side mitigation steps so docs can be added to developer guides.
